note: Independent source rejudgment after the comment-only errcheck annotation on the hard-expiry timeout join. RFC 4301 section 4.4.2.1 says: Lifetime of this SA: a time interval after which an SA must be replaced with a new SA (and new SPI) or terminated, plus an indication of which of these actions should occur. All four tagged units were re-read against newLifetimeState, softExpired, hardExpired and maintainSA, including its rekey trigger and cleanup. The interval pair pins configured duration, replace-before-terminate, neither action before expiry and termination at the hard boundary. The owner-loop pair isolates soft and hard expiry: soft initiates CREATE_CHILD_SA with a new nonzero inbound SPI for the old Child SA and no timeout; hard returns errTimeout, leaves no pending rekey or Child SA, removes the old inbound SPI and sends no request. Removing termination or swapping the actions violates these exact assertions. The edited timeout path still fails unconditionally; no input, assertion or RFC claim changed. Prior proof provenance retained: the existing discrimination record carries revert observations for maintainSA and newLifetimeState; the previous audit additionally reported the author's soft/hard-swap overlay turning both action tests red. Those are historical observations, not executions by this judge. Discrimination records are unchanged. No runtime rerun, build, lint or RFC check was performed for this source-only rejudgment.
